what: Grades of every answer in evaluation/per_question_results.json against the ground-truth answers in evaluation/eval_set.json. RAGAs faithfulness and answer relevancy do not use the ground truth, so these grades were added to check correctness.

grader.panels: Two panels, both the same model (claude-opus-5) run twice with the same rubric and a different instruction per panel. Each panel was 7 separate agents grading 4 questions each (all 5 configurations per question).
grader.panel_a_instruction: Your lens: strict specification accuracy. Check each listed field name, enum value and cardinality against ground_truth one by one.
grader.panel_b_instruction: Your lens: fabrication hunting. Assume answers may sound confident while being invented; look for claims about other protocols (ACPI, OAuth, PXE, OCPP 2.0 terminology), invented numbers, and required/optional mix-ups. Do not give credit for fluent but unsupported text.
grader.independence: The panels ran in parallel as separate agents and did not see each other's grades.
grader.not_blind_to: Configuration. Each grader saw all five answers to a question side by side, labelled by configuration name, together with the retrieved chunks and the RAGAs scores (the prompt said to ignore the scores).
grader.rubric:
Grades (pick exactly one per answer):
- Answerable questions (type is lookup, multipart or cross_section):
  correct   = states every element of ground_truth and asserts nothing that contradicts it or the spec.
  partial   = some ground_truth elements present but others missing, OR all present plus a material wrong claim
              (e.g. calling an optional field required, extra invented enum values).
  incorrect = ground_truth elements absent or contradicted, including answers about a different protocol or domain.
  declined  = says the context/it cannot answer, without asserting a wrong answer.
  (never use hallucinated for answerable questions; use incorrect)
- Unanswerable questions (type is unanswerable):
  correct      = says the specification does not specify it (or equivalent), without inventing a value/behaviour.
  partial      = says it is not specified but ALSO offers a specific invented value/behaviour as if typical or required.
  hallucinated = asserts a specific timeout, number or mandated behaviour as if OCPP 1.6 specifies it.
  declined     = only says the given context lacks the information, without saying the spec does not define it.
retrieval_contains_answer (judge ONLY the retrieved_contexts, not the answer):
  yes/partial/no for fixed_256, fixed_512, fixed_1024, semantic on answerable questions;
  na for no_retrieval, and na for every unanswerable question.
rationale: one short sentence quoting or naming the decisive evidence.
Grade against ground_truth as written. If retrieved_contexts clearly contradict ground_truth, still grade against
ground_truth but add an entry to ground_truth_concerns quoting the contradicting context.

ground_truth_concerns_raised_by_graders.concern: This does not change the ground truth, but the fixed_512 context has a spec inconsistency. The sequence diagram writes 'StopTransaction.req(meterStop, timestamp, transactionId, reason, [idTag], [transactionData])' with reason unbracketed, which suggests it is mandatory. The field table in the fixed_1024 context says 'reason Reason 0..1 Optional'. The ground truth (meterStop, timestamp, transactionId) follows the authoritative table.

The question and ground truth call "connectorId > 0" the stated constraint. The 6.31 context actually has a constraint column reading "connectorId >= 0"; ">0" appears only in the description ("This contains a number (>0) designating a connector of the Charge Point."). The second part of the ground truth matches the description, not the constraint, and it restates the question's premise rather than adding anything to the answer. Answers were graded mainly on naming the main powermeter.

The retrieved Figure 21 and Figure 8 sequence diagrams read 'StopTransaction.req(meterStop, timestamp, transactionId, reason, [idTag], [transactionData])' and show reason unbracketed, which suggests it is required. The ground truth follows the 6.49 table ('reason Reason 0..1 Optional'), which is the authoritative field definition, so the spec contradicts itself here. Models reading only the diagram can reasonably treat reason as required.

The ground-truth phrase 'an omitted Reason SHOULD be assumed to be Local' comes from section 4.10, which none of the configs retrieved; the retrieved text only has the 6.49 wording 'MAY only be omitted when the Reason is "Local"'. Also, 7.36 calls both Local and Remote a 'regular termination'. So 'normal termination' in the question is ambiguous and could wrongly suggest remote stops default to Local.

The retrieved section 4.10 sequence diagram shows 'StopTransaction.req(meterStop, timestamp, transactionId, reason, [idTag], [transactionData])' without brackets on reason, which suggests reason is required. The ground truth follows the 6.49 table, where reason is 0..1. This inconsistency inside the spec probably misled several answers. The ground truth's 'transactionData (optional)' is also less precise than the table's 0..* ('a container for any number of MeterValues').

spec_source '4.1-4.10, pp.33-47' does not point to the relevant text. fixed_256 retrieved an OCPP-J passage: 'an implementation-dependent timeout interval has elapsed since the message was sent. Implementations are free to choose this timeout interval'. That passage agrees with the ground truth, but it shows the corpus holds transport-level timeout guidance, so a correct answer could cite it instead of simply saying 'not specified'.

Not a real error in the ground truth, but the spec contradicts itself here and it misleads models. The fixed_512 and fixed_1024 contexts quote the Figure 21 sequence diagram 'StopTransaction.req(meterStop, timestamp, transactionId, reason, [idTag], [transactionData])', where reason is not bracketed and so looks required. The 6.49 field table (also in the fixed_1024 context) says 'reason Reason 0..1 Optional'. The ground truth follows the table and is correct; the diagram probably explains why fixed_512 called reason required.

The question says "despite the stated connectorId > 0 constraint", but in every retrieved 6.31 chunk the constraint column reads "connectorId >= 0". Only the description says "a number (>0) designating a connector". The ground truth phrase "the same field definition also states connectorId > 0" holds only for the description text, so the premise about the constraint is imprecise.

The retrieved Figure 21 diagram, 'StopTransaction.req(meterStop, timestamp, transactionId, reason, [idTag], [transactionData])', shows reason without brackets, as if required. The 6.49 table says 'reason Reason 0..1 Optional'. The ground truth (reason optional) follows the table, so answers that rely on the diagram can call reason required. This is an inconsistency inside the spec, not an error in the ground truth.

The same Figure 21 diagram inconsistency applies here: reason appears unbracketed ('transactionId, reason, [idTag]') while table 6.49 marks it 0..1 Optional. Separately, none of the retrieval configs surfaced the 4.10 sentence saying an omitted Reason SHOULD be assumed Local, so that part of the ground truth could not be grounded in any retrieved context.

The ground truth marks reason optional, which matches the 6.49 field table (Reason 0..1). But the 4.10 sequence diagram in the retrieved context (fixed_512, semantic) reads 'StopTransaction.req(meterStop, timestamp, transactionId, reason, [idTag], [transactionData])', with reason unbracketed, which implies it is required. The spec contradicts itself here, and answers grounded only in the diagram will call reason required. The ground truth also says 'optional' for transactionData, whose actual cardinality is 0..*.
